class_name: 授受-内の受益-テモラウ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Frames an event as a benefit the receiver obtained, with the receiver as subject and the person who acts marked with に (から when something is handed over or told): 兄に自転車を直してもらった. てくれる reports the same favor with the giver as subject, and ていただく is the humble version used when the actor outranks you. The beneficiary need not be the speaker: 弟は先輩に直してもらった is fine.

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]に自転車[じてんしゃ]のパンクを直[なお]してもらった。
examples.english: I had my older brother fix the flat on my bike.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]めに医者[いしゃ]に傷[きず]を見[み]てもらうつもりだ。
examples.english: I mean to get a doctor to look at the cut before long.

examples.ruby: 駅前[えきまえ]の店[みせ]で時計[とけい]の電池[でんち]を交換[こうかん]してもらった。
examples.english: I had the shop by the station swap the battery in my watch.

patterns.usage_note: The humble counterpart of てもらう: the receiver is the subject and the person doing the favor outranks them (先生に読んでいただいた). てくださる puts that other person in the subject slot instead, so keep one perspective per sentence. 〜ていただけますか and 〜ていただけませんか are the standard business request forms, and the auxiliary is usually written in kana rather than 頂く or 戴く.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]に卒業論文[そつぎょうろんぶん]を読[よ]んでいただいた。
examples.english: I was fortunate enough to have my professor read my thesis.

examples.ruby: 来週[らいしゅう]、部長[ぶちょう]に空港[くうこう]まで送[おく]っていただきます。
examples.english: Next week the department head will be good enough to drive me to the airport.

examples.ruby: 近所[きんじょ]の方[かた]に留守中[るすちゅう]の郵便[ゆうびん]を預[あず]かっていただいた。
examples.english: A neighbor was kind enough to hold my mail while I was away.
